center.locator: centroid of the convex hull of the 300 OSM tank footprints (geometry:hawc-tank-field-hull)
center.note: Map centre only; not a claim about any structure. Lies 0.6 km from the HAWC paper's rounded site coordinate (18.99 N, 97.31 W, good to 0.01 degree), as it should.

levels.name: Surface
levels.note: The array is entirely at the surface, on a levelled platform.

name: HAWC — Sierra Negra
notes: Tank positions are OpenStreetMap footprints (300 ways traced together in 2017), read with the OSM API map call on 2026-10-25 because Overpass answered 502 at capacity. The tank count (300), the field area (hull 22.4 thousand m2 against the paper's 22,000 and 22,395 m2) and the summed tank area (13.1 thousand m2 against 12.6 thousand m2 for 300 circles of 7.3 m) all match the HAWC paper.

The 345 outrigger tanks (1.55 m diameter, 'concentric circular symmetric' around the main array, 12 to 18 m apart; arXiv:1908.06650) are not drawn: no fetched source gives their positions and OSM has none of them. Backlog: the outrigger layout table or GIS from the HAWC collaboration.

The HAWC Utility Building ('installed East to the tank array platform') and the counting house have no named OSM polygon; the LMT on the Sierra Negra summit is a separate facility about 1.3 km to the south-west and is not drawn.
site:hawc-sierra-negra carries the paper's coordinate rounded to 0.01 degree (precision_m 600); a tighter position could be derived from the layout of the tank field, but none is recorded.

summary.plain: The HAWC water-Cherenkov gamma-ray observatory of 300 water tanks on the Sierra Negra volcano, Puebla, Mexico, drawn tank by tank.
summary.technical: The 300 tank footprints come from OpenStreetMap and are checked by summed area against 300 circles of the published 7.3 m diameter; the tank-field outline is their convex hull, checked against the published 22,000 m2 array area and the 22,395 m2 platform. Map centre is the hull centroid.
